title: Pinning policy: fallbacks, customer mapping & telemetry cookbook
content:
Purpose:
This is a working cookbook for how we map customers to region pins, what fallback behaviors we accept, and the telemetry + operator steps to detect and remediate mis-pinning. The goal is to provide concrete examples operators and Solutions Engineers can follow when a customer has mixed residency requirements or when region capacity is constrained.

Audience:
- SRE/OPS oncall
- Solutions Engineers during onboarding
- Product owners that define acceptable fallbacks

Summary / TL;DR:
- Primary pin decision = declared residency > billing country > cloud region of customer-managed bucket > IP geolocation (last resort).
- Acceptable fallback hierarchy (for strict customers): same-country > same-region (e.g., eu-west) > non-prod fallback with encryption-at-rest + KMS in customer region.
- For less strict customers fallback to compatible model variant in other region with audited KV-clearing on cross-border access.

1) Customer mapping cookbook (practical examples)
Example A: EU enterprise with explicit GDPR residency request in contract (contract clause: data_residency=EU)
- Pin: eu-central-1 (customer selected region catalog)
- Storage: customer-managed S3 in eu-central-1 (preferred). If they provide no bucket, create dedicated bucket in eu-central-1 and enable SSE-KMS with their KMS alias.
- Fallback policy: never spill to non-EU. If capacity unavailable escalate to capacity team and trigger negotiated burst allocation.
- Telemetry: tag customer.requests with pin_enforced=true, pin_reason=contract, pin_region=eu-central-1

Example B: Mid-market US customer, billing country US, no explicit residency requirement
- Pin: us-east-1 by default
- Fallback policy: allow cross-region in contiguous US regions (us-east-1 <-> us-east-2) for capacity reasons, prefer same cloud provider.
- Telemetry: pin_reason=billing, allowed_fallbacks="us-east-2,us-west-2"

Example C: Startup with hybrid requirement: embeddings must remain in EU but inference can run in hosted US (customer provides EU embeddings store)
- Pin: split policy - dataset pins vs compute pins. Create data_pin=eu-central-1, compute_pin=hosted-us-east-1. Enforce KV cache eviction after any cross-region transfer and record audit event.
- Telemetry keys: "data_pin", "compute_pin", "cross_region_transfer=true/false"

2) Fallback heuristics and safe defaults
- Never override explicit contract clauses. Contract wins.
- For onboarding boolean flags: if customer_residency_flag is present, treat as authoritative unless legal requests otherwise.
- When capacity shortage occurs: attempt same-country region first, then same-continent region. For intercontinental moves, only if customer has opted-in to cross-border fallback.
- During emergency fallback (SLA threat), automatically choose nearest compatible model variant and mark session as degraded_mode. Notify SRE page and customer.

3) Operator runbook snippets (quick actions)
- Check pin status: QUERY: SELECT customer_id, pin_region, pin_reason, last_pin_enforce_ts FROM residency_pins WHERE customer_id = "<id>";
- Force re-pin (temporary) via admin-tool: admin.pin_customer("<id>", "eu-central-1", ttl=3600, reason="manual-ops-repin");
- Clear KV caches across regions after re-pin: run script ops/clear_kv_cache.sh --customer <id> --regions "us-east-1,eu-central-1"
- Escalation: if admin-pin fails due to capacity, open INC with team 'capacity' and attach job id + telemetry snapshot.

4) Telemetry and alerting (concrete names)
- residency.pin.enforce_attempt (counter) -> labels: customer_id, pin_region, pin_reason, result (success|fail)
- residency.pin.fallback (counter) -> labels: customer_id, from_region, to_region, fallback_type (capacity|policy|operator)
- residency.cross_region_transfer (event) -> labels: data_type (embeddings|kv|request_payload), bytes, source_region, dest_region, customer_id
- alerts:
  - residency.pin.failures.rate > 5/min -> alert SRE (pager)
  - cross_region_transfer where data_type=embeddings and dest_region not in customer.allowed_regions -> page legal + product

Recommended dashboards (minimal):
- Pin enforcement success rate by region (last 24h)
- Cross-region transfer stream (last 7 days) with customer_id and bytes transferred
- Capacity vs. pin demand heatmap (predictive)

5) Config examples (YAML style for routing policy)
- NOTE: this is an ops-level example, not the production schema.
routing_policy:
  - match: { customer_attribute: contract.residency, value: "EU" }
    action: { pin_region: "eu-central-1", enforce: true }
  - match: { customer_attribute: billing.country, value: "US" }
    action: { pin_region: "us-east-1", enforce: false, allowed_fallbacks: ["us-east-2"] }
  - match: { customer_attribute: data_type, value: "embeddings" }
    action: { pin_region: "data_pin", separate_compute: true }

6) Audit and evidence we attach to contracts
- For customers with strict residency we produce an evidentiary bundle: pin_manifest.json (signed), S3 bucket ARN, KMS alias, last 30 days of residency.pin.enforce_attempt logs filtered by customer_id.
- Make sure legal receives cross_region_transfer events with full headers for any transfers that touch PII.

7) Open questions / design decisions to resolve
- Should we allow automated intercontinental fallback for non-PII payloads after X minutes of queueing? (tradeoff latency vs compliance risk)
- How strict should split-pinning be for multi-tenant models that share cache? Need architectural note from serving-runtime on cache partitioning guarantees. -> @Arjun to follow up with runtime team (GH-289).
- Standard TTL for manual admin pin (3600s?) propose 1 hour by default.

8) Rollout plan for new stricter enforcement toggle (prod flag = "residency.strict_mode")
- Phase 0 (dev): smoke tests in staging with synthetic customers (1 day)
- Phase 1 (canary): enable for internal alpha customers only (1 week)
- Phase 2 (gradual): opt-in customers + new enterprise signups (2 weeks)
- Phase 3 (global): enable for all new traffic, existing customers must opt-out via formal request (4 weeks)
- Metrics to watch: pin.enforce.success_rate, latent.queue_time_by_pin, cross_region_transfer.events_by_customer

9) Customer-facing notes (for Solutions Engineers)
- When we recommend a pin, explain: "We will keep your data and KV cache in <region>. If we must run inference outside <region> due to emergencies, we'll notify you and clear any cached state on the other region within 1 hour."
- For multi-region customers provide a one-page "residency manifest" during onboarding.

10) Quick checklist for onboarding with residency requirements
- [ ] Confirm contract clause and canonical customer residency flag
- [ ] Validate customer-managed storage + KMS or propose dedicated bucket
- [ ] Confirm allowed fallback regions and escalation contacts
- [ ] Create pin in Residency DB with pin_reason and attach contract id
- [ ] Run canary requests and verify telemetry events for that customer

Appendix: useful links and ops snippets
- Slack thread: #residency-ops (link pinned message id: 5623)
- Jira: ENG-4823 (pinning automation), ENG-5100 (cross-region telemetry work)
- GH: routing-config PR 127 (example policy)
- Script: ops/clear_kv_cache.sh (used in re-pin flows)

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally pragmatic and contains both policy and operator-level commands. Goal is to converge on authoritative fallback hierarchy and the minimal telemetry we need to make enforcement auditable.
- Please add edge cases you have seen oncall (timing, partial drafts of contracts, third-party storage references).

Unresolved TODOs:
- [ ] Add canonical SQL migration to add "allowed_fallbacks" column to residency_pins table (db team)
- [ ] Produce a one-page customer "residency manifest" template for SEs (marketing/legal)
- [ ] Confirm KMS integration flow for on-prem HSMs (security)
